attrs.text: Browser sign-in requires the Host webServer. Only local access and SSH local forwarding through HTTP localhost, 127.0.0.1, or [::1] with an explicit port are supported; non-loopback reverse proxies are unsupported. Account tokens have no expiry or refresh flow; explicit DSH sign-out removes the local grant before calling POST /auth-api/v0/users/logout in the background. Remote failures never restore local login. The captured old token receives at most five additional attempts with exponential delays of 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 seconds by default; logoutMaxRetries (0–5) and logoutRetryDelayMs configure that policy. Each request uses requestTimeoutMs. Provider shutdown aborts requests and waits, and pending revocations are not persisted. Local credential deletion failures remain visible to the caller. Authorization-attempt deadlines still apply before a token is issued. Cancellation or timeout after initialization sends one background POST /auth-api/v0/dsh/auth_cancel with the authorize_id from auth_init.biz_data and the original code_verifier, without account authorization. Local cancellation never waits for this request or reverses on failure; requestTimeoutMs bounds it, and provider shutdown aborts it. title: Only the reachability of a Git target's host is checked before the installed copy is removed, and only through Git: a host that only pnpm's own proxy settings reach is refused as unreachable. A target whose commit is missing, that needs cre...

attrs.text: Only the reachability of a Git target's host is checked before the installed copy is removed, and only through Git: a host that only pnpm's own proxy settings reach is refused as unreachable. A target whose commit is missing, that needs credentials pnpm lacks, declares no bundle, rejects the running DSH, or installs another package or version costs a stop and a reinstallation. The reinstallation uses the saved spec, from which the user information of an http(s) URL was removed, so a private repository needs a Git credential helper or the SSH form. A copy the SSH fallback saved for an HTTPS URL with a port loses the port, so its origin no longer matches the index's HTTPS spec and its updates are refused.

title: The Git transport probe keeps the parent console on Windows, so an SSH host-key or passphrase prompt can appear in the launching terminal until `gitTransportTimeoutMs`. On POSIX a host missing from `known_hosts` fails the SSH probe, so inst...

attrs.text: The Git transport probe keeps the parent console on Windows, so an SSH host-key or passphrase prompt can appear in the launching terminal until `gitTransportTimeoutMs`. On POSIX a host missing from `known_hosts` fails the SSH probe, so installation stays on HTTPS until the host key is accepted once, for example with `ssh -T git@<host>`. A credential-helper dialog or ssh-agent confirmation, such as a Touch ID or `ssh-add -c` dialog, that takes longer than the deadline counts as a failed probe, and an HTTPS probe that times out lets a reachable SSH form be saved to the profile. A private repository waits up to twice `gitTransportTimeoutMs` before pnpm starts. The SSH form always uses the `git` user and SSH's default port; other SSH endpoints need a `url.<base>.insteadOf` rule. When both probes fail, the diagnostic is pnpm's HTTPS failure; the SSH probe's reason is not reported.

If a dependency upgrade removes that rule, loading the grammar throws and Go code renders as plain text; delete the patch once `@shikijs/langs` ships the upstream rule.

title: **The Perl match rule is patched locally** — when the Perl grammar loads, its bare `/…/` match rule also begins after `,`, `!`, `=`, `=>` and after `split`, `grep`, `and`, `or`, `not`, `return`, `while` and `until`, because the vendored rul...

attrs.text: **The Perl match rule is patched locally** — when the Perl grammar loads, its bare `/…/` match rule also begins after `,`, `!`, `=`, `=>` and after `split`, `grep`, `and`, `or`, `not`, `return`, `while` and `until`, because the vendored rule treats a pattern such as `split /^---\s*$/m, $text` as code and colors the rest of the source as a string. These words and `if`/`unless` count only when no identifier character, sigil, `>`, `:` or `-` precedes them, so `$split / 2` and `$obj->return / 2` are divisions. A `/` elsewhere, such as after `?`, `[` or `print`, still reads as division. The upstream [textmate/perl.tmbundle](https://github.com/textmate/perl.tmbundle) grammar has the same rule. If a dependency upgrade changes that rule, loading the grammar throws and Perl code renders as plain text.

The changes tab shows no plugin lenses, annotations, toolbar, file-menu, or comment-form entries, whose extension points name a Session, and its quotes go to the chat's draft instead of the Session's input. The chat starts in the Workspace's shared blank Session, which New Session also shows, and does not check that the Workspace is a checkout of the repository; the change request to bind waits in Host memory until the first message, so a Host restart forgets it. Pending review comments last while the page shows their change request.

attrs.text: **Timing is derived, not sampled.** Total time is the last step's end minus the first step's start; queueing and scheduler waits land in the "rest" segment. The total-time bar draws tool calls as the union of their paired intervals, so parallel calls count once; the tool column keeps the summed per-call time. A turn bar is scaled against the turns currently visible on screen, so a much larger turn that scrolled away does not flatten the rows in view.

attrs.text: The Owner Host and worker ship together. The supervisor mints a branded UUID `registrationToken` per logical add, invalidates it on removal, and replays it only for the same retained registration after process restart. Lifecycle, requests, and cancellations echo that token with the share id; per-request `TunnelRequestToken` remains independent. IPC decoders refuse missing identities, and neither token enters Relay URLs or wire frames. Same-package IPC does not negotiate versions; Relay wire frames retain numeric ids and protocol version 1. Compatibility capabilities include `actor-credential` and `direct-connection`. An actor may also carry an optional `displayName` (presentation data only, used for attribution; authorization keeps using the identity triple), and an optional owner-verifiable `credential` (the protocol validates its type only; an owner verifies it before trusting the asserted identity, and absence keeps today's Relay-asserted semantics). A share spec may carry `connection`; absence reads as `{ mode: 'relay' }`, and a Relay that still owns the data path refuses a `direct` registration.

The worker forwards snapshots only from its current socket; the Host clears authority on socket loss and refreshes the authenticated requests snapshot before external execution admission. An unavailable snapshot fails closed instead of borrowing persisted ACLs.

These checks preserve recorded fields and explicit refusals, not a per-release translation or an unbounded support window.

It still imports a credential, which is its own sign-in, but that import claims and re-registers nothing. The global switch is `none` (open nothing), `custom` (follow the per-plugin list), or `all` (open every method the live catalog offers). Each plugin is then off, all its methods, or a subset; a partial selection stores an explicit method list, so methods the catalog adds later stay closed until the owner saves again. Plugin rows use the package's localized title when one exists and otherwise fall back to the package segment or namespace; search and bounded scrolling keep a large catalog usable. The selection is share-wide: every admitted viewer may call a selected method on the resources the policy binds, and per-viewer method levels are not established. Method authorization is independent of the session tier; the core share roles still decide Session and Workspace calls. A selection naming a method the catalog no longer offers exposes nothing but stays stored until the owner saves again.

title: **Provider HTTP status is unavailable** — pi-ai error events do not expose a stable HTTP status across providers, so failures are classified from the error text. When a message leads with a 4xx or 5xx status, as Anthropic and OpenAI SDK err...

attrs.text: **Provider HTTP status is unavailable** — pi-ai error events do not expose a stable HTTP status across providers, so failures are classified from the error text. When a message leads with a 4xx or 5xx status, as Anthropic and OpenAI SDK errors do, the status rules read only that status. Other formats, such as `Mistral API error (<status>): <body>`, still match a status quoted anywhere in the message, and the quota, rate-limit, and invalid-request wording rules read the whole message, so a gateway 5xx that relays an upstream `insufficient_quota` or `invalid_request_error` becomes a non-retryable `QUOTA` or `INVALID_REQUEST` failure.

attrs.text: **Streamed JSON tool-call arguments avoid per-delta reparsing** — the installed pi-ai carries [`patches/@earendil-works__pi-ai@1.3.0.patch`](../../../patches/@earendil-works__pi-ai@1.3.0.patch), which removes the per-delta re-parse of the whole accumulated argument JSON in every stream adapter (upstream [earendil-works/pi#9265](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/9265)); unpatched, a multi-megabyte argument stream costs O(n²) CPU on the event loop and stalls every session in the process. Completion events supply parsed arguments; Responses may parse at both argument completion and output-item completion. This adapter reads only delta strings and finalized arguments. Re-apply or retire the patch on every pi-ai upgrade.

The digest covers the pi-ai context objects, not the wire body: switching authentication or wire-changing compat settings mid-conversation is not detected, a pi-ai upgrade that changes Anthropic message serialization requires a new `DIGEST_SEED` in [`src/prefix-binding.ts`](src/prefix-binding.ts), and any change to how this package builds those objects drops recorded thinking once.

title: **Provider-native discovery answers through this plugin's ambient context** — a route naming no credential defers to the catalog provider's own resolution, which asks for environment values (`AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AWS_PROFILE`, and each p...

attrs.text: **Provider-native discovery answers through this plugin's ambient context** — a route naming no credential defers to the catalog provider's own resolution, which asks for environment values (`AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY`, `AWS_PROFILE`, and each provider's own set) and for local credential files. Both questions are answered here: the credential seam is consulted before the process environment, and file existence is checked against the host process's filesystem with `~` expanded. What it cannot do is *read* a credential file's contents — a provider that parses `~/.aws/credentials` itself does so directly, outside the seam.

title: **Tool updates require session history** — `GenerateOptions.tools` contains active definitions. `toolHistory` supplies the initial declarations and historically resolved additions from `Session.toolHistory()`. At adapter dispatch, `projectT...

attrs.text: **Tool updates require session history** — `GenerateOptions.tools` contains active definitions. `toolHistory` supplies the initial declarations and historically resolved additions from `Session.toolHistory()`. At adapter dispatch, `projectToolUpdates` constructs deferred declarations and retains removed definitions for `in-history`; `addition-only` omits removed definitions and removal messages. Removing any tool or adding tools to an empty set on an addition-only route rebuilds the baseline from the declarations available after that update. Deferred declarations count as existing tools. Superseded tool blocks are omitted while unrelated content survives; subsequent additions remain deferred. Unsupported routes receive active tools without developer messages or `deferLoading`. Missing history or a request prefix omitting recorded updates falls back to current declarations without developer messages. Explicitly deferred tools become immediate during a rebuild only if an addition has already activated them; unactivated declarations remain deferred.

title: **Await lowering relaxes declaration semantics** — in transformed programs, top-level `let`, `const`, and `class` bindings are mutable and initialized to `undefined` before execution; the native temporal dead zone does not apply. Function d...

attrs.text: **Await lowering relaxes declaration semantics** — in transformed programs, top-level `let`, `const`, and `class` bindings are mutable and initialized to `undefined` before execution; the native temporal dead zone does not apply. Function declarations populate retained globals when execution reaches them, and a `var` declaration without an initializer resets its binding to `undefined`. Direct-eval declarations stay within that evaluation. Top-level `using` declarations are rejected; put disposable bindings inside a block. Runtime stack locations refer to the transformed source. Scripts that compile without lowering keep native semantics.

title: **Scoped REPL copies values when a call starts** — with `replScoped` omitted or `true`, assignments that earlier code makes afterwards stay invisible to later calls, and a `let`, `const` or `class` redeclaration cannot read the earlier valu...

attrs.text: **Scoped REPL copies values when a call starts** — with `replScoped` omitted or `true`, assignments that earlier code makes afterwards stay invisible to later calls, and a `let`, `const` or `class` redeclaration cannot read the earlier value of its own name. A `var` redeclaration starts from that value, so `var count = count + 1` adds to it, also after an earlier `let` or `const` of the same name. Relative `import()` specifiers keep resolving from the environment's first working directory after a later call changes directory; relative file access follows the current directory. The `codeGeneration` limit rejects only the program context's own `eval`, `Function` and WebAssembly compilation and is no isolation: main-realm functions copied into the context, such as `setTimeout.constructor`, still compile code. Columns after the inserted completion on the final expression's line shift right by 17, programs that start with `#!` or contain `__$binding_` anywhere are rejected, binding-global and error-class names containing that prefix fail before process launch, and a surviving function keeps every value copied into its call. The [scoped REPL decision](../../../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-11-09-retained-ptc-scoped-repl.md) lists the complete behavior.

attrs.text: **One live writer per session** — the write-handle claim excludes a second writer inside the owning backend instance, and a kernel lock (non-blocking `flock(2)` on `session.lock`; on Windows a named kernel semaphore derived from that path, with no filesystem footprint) excludes every other instance and process; the lock is taken at write-open of an existing artifact and, for a created session, only right before its first materializing write, so an unmaterialized session leaves no filesystem footprint. A crashed holder's lock dies with its process, so its session is writable again immediately, while a live-but-wedged holder blocks writers until its process exits (on POSIX, removing the lock file forfeits that exclusion; release itself never removes it). Advisory `flock` is unreliable on some network filesystems (NFSv3), and the Windows semaphore name is per login session.

attrs.text: **Language mode and named-pipe capture under the Windows sandbox** — under the [Windows ACL sandbox](../../sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/README.md), read-only pwsh starts in ConstrainedLanguage because its temp write denial makes PowerShell's AppLocker probe fail closed: `Add-Type`, non-core .NET statics (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors, and the mode cannot be lifted from inside. Workspace-write's private temp lets the probe complete, so it stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. title: **Native selection has bounded per-spawn costs** — Linux checks the bootstrap entry, libc `execve`/`fcntl` bindings, reachable user manager, and literal-argv scope probe on the first eligible ordinary or terminal spawn and keeps that verdic...

attrs.text: **Native selection has bounded per-spawn costs** — Linux checks the bootstrap entry, libc `execve`/`fcntl` bindings, reachable user manager, and literal-argv scope probe on the first eligible ordinary or terminal spawn and keeps that verdict, including a failed or timed-out probe. The user manager is identified by the process listening on `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/private`, the socket `systemd-run --user` connects through, as listed in the kernel's unix socket table (`/proc/net/unix`) for the same network namespace; reading the table costs time proportional to its size. After a positive verdict, each eligible spawn probes again when the `systemd-run` found through `PATH` has a different device, inode, size, or modification time, and otherwise confirms the manager: a listener confirms it without a child process; otherwise one `systemctl --user show` query decides, and that spawn uses the fallback when the query fails. A scope launch whose bootstrap never consumed its launch request, such as one sent to a hung manager that still listens, fails that command, as do scope launches issued before that failure arrives, and the next eligible spawn probes again. After a negative verdict, the provider probes again only when a different listener appears, so a manager that starts later is used without a restart. Windows rechecks the runner entry, bindings, and current Job support before every ordinary spawn. Fallback-warning de-duplication also persists for the provider lifetime. All prob...

title: **There is no batch-wide native-search counter** — `searchMaxQueries` bounds `ctx.web.search` calls, but a provider may perform several native searches inside each call; for example a model-backed provider configured with `maxUses` can perm...

title: **No availability observation** — `listProviders()` and `web/providers-changed` report which providers are registered, not whether they are usable; there is no capability-status query, and `searchReady()` and `fetchReady()` report only the ...

Availability is observable only by running a search or fetch and routing the thrown code, and the no-provider failure is the generic `WEB_PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` with no per-provider reason enumeration ([Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/archived/simplification/2026-07-04-drop-unconsumed-web-observation-surface.md)).

attrs.statedReason: Cross-platform boundary for the persistent PTY backend, including ConPTY on Windows. Pulled in by @earendil-works/pi-ai (optional LLM API backend). pnpm lists them only because they ship lifecycle scripts, but those are no-ops we don't need, so we deny them — install still succeeds. JSONL durability calls MoveFileExW with write-through publication on Windows. Consumers pin 3.1.1: Koffi 3.3.2's source build fails under GCC 13 when optional prebuilts are omitted. Upgrade all consumers together after the replacement passes that build and the release packed-install check. The Python runtime deploy includes the reviewed workspace postinstall that restores the executable bit on node-pty's macOS spawn helper.
